title: Session restart on a new host: contamination diagnosis, an infra bug fix, and a mechanism-only planning paper
abstract: The prior session's execution host became unreachable (host key changed) and was replaced by a fresh account on a different physical machine (zp-nc71) with eight idle H200s, no prior torch environment, and no cached training data. This report covers the restart period: diagnosing that the registered baseline in reconciliation.json v31 is contaminated by a prior session's throughput collapse, fixing a real portability bug in lib.py that silently redirected data loading to an unreachable path from a different user account, standing up the environment (torch 2.13.0+cu130, all 11 data shards, a freshly trained BPE tokenizer), and producing paper_021 -- a planning paper proposing six MECHANISM-only experiments (the plateau rule forbids further knob experiments this block) with a central finding, corroborated independently by two proposer agents and verified in source, that the n-gram sparse optimizer decays its entire state tensor every step because of a stale comment written for a now-dormant frame. No gated experiment has yet run this period; this report is infra and diagnosis, not a results report, and its findings are recorded at the assessment levels the evidence actually supports.
methods: Diagnosis of the contaminated baseline was direct arithmetic: the registered baseline.per_seed values in research/setup/reconciliation.json (mean 0.934930, n=10) were compared against the same configuration's paired-run values recorded in campaign_log.jsonl from an earlier, uncontended session (mean 0.929541, n=10), a gap of +0.005390. The contaminating session's own run records (research/experiments/runs/runs.jsonl, experiment_ids matching docmask_provenance and block22) show num_steps clustering near 1147 in 45 of 48 runs against an expected ~2000 for the same 300s wall-clock budget, consistent with GPU contention from over-launching concurrent arms. The lib.py bug was found by running a smoke-test training step on the new host and tracing a PermissionError back to lib.py's DATA_DIR resolution, which trusted os.path.isdir('/data') without checking the directory actually contained usable files -- on this shared host /data is a leftover, unwritable symlink farm from a different (unreachable) account. The mechanism proposals in paper_021 were generated by two independent proposer agents (kernel/throughput lens and architecture/memory lens) reasoning from the actual train.py source plus the campaign's own recorded evidence, then screened by inline adversarial critique that eliminated two proposals on a logistics fact (github.com is unreachable from this host, blocking FlashAttention-4 and Lngram installation) discovered while writing the paper.

findings.statement: The baseline registered in research/setup/reconciliation.json v31 (0.934930, n=10) is contaminated: the same fa3-varlen-doc-mask configuration measured on an uncontended host in an earlier session gives 0.929541 (n=10), a gap of +0.005390 in the wrong direction, and 45 of 48 runs in the contaminating session completed approximately 1147 optimizer steps against an expected approximately 2000 for the same 300s budget.
limitations: This is a direct comparison of two already-recorded aggregates, not a fresh controlled experiment; it has not yet been promoted to formal internal_run evidence with a registered analysis record.

The clean 0.929541 comparison figure itself derives from direct-SSH runs predating the formal authorize-run harness and is therefore weak provenance, not adoption-grade evidence, per the campaign's own known standing gaps.

A full re-reconciliation (fresh reference-code hash, fresh frozen_files digests, and a genuine >=10-seed baseline remeasurement through authorize-run) is required before any new baseline number can be adopted; this report does not attempt to hand-edit reconciliation.json's baseline field.

findings.statement: lib.py's DATA_DIR resolution used os.path.isdir('/data') as its only check for whether to trust an upstream data mount. On the new execution host, /data exists as a leftover directory owned by a different, now-unreachable user account, containing only a broken symlink at /data/tokenizer -> /home/user/.cache/autoresearch/tokenizer. This silently redirected all data and tokenizer loading to an unusable path and raised PermissionError only once tokenizer loading was actually attempted, well after RESOLVED_CONFIG had already printed and the run appeared to be progressing normally.
limitations: Fixed by requiring os.path.isfile of the actual tokenizer file rather than directory existence; verified locally that DATA_DIR now resolves to the account's own cache directory on the new host.

This changes lib.py's SHA-256, which is one of the frozen_files reconciliation.json tracks, so it is folded into the full re-reconciliation this period's blockers require rather than reconciled in isolation.

findings.statement: paper_021 (AI_papers/paper_021_the_stale_comment_20260730.tex) proposes six MECHANISM experiments, each with a numeric falsifier and seven-axis novelty/provenance/validity/impact/reliability/feasibility/falsifiability scoring. Its lead proposal targets train.py:2547-2548, a comment stating that optimizer step-time cost does not affect val_bpb under STOP_MODE=steps -- true of the campaign's dormant fixed-step frame, false under the only live wall-clock frame -- which left a full-table state decay unoptimized in the sparse n-gram RMSProp path (train.py:2572, 2579-2581), predicted at roughly 19ms per step against a previously unexplained 15.0ms batch-independent term in the campaign's own throughput model.
limitations: This is a planning document; none of its six proposals have been run. The predicted effect sizes are derived from the campaign's own token-throughput law and from first-principles bandwidth arithmetic, not from a new measurement.

Two proposals in the original two-agent slate (FlashAttention-4 on Hopper; Lngram latent-code memory) were dropped by adversarial critique on a logistics finding -- github.com is unreachable from the execution host -- rather than on a scientific defect, and should be reconsidered if a mirror becomes available.

negative_results: get-pip.py bootstrap failed (truncated download); replaced with a miniforge/pip-from-source path.
github.com is unreachable from the execution host (connection timed out after 129s); PyPI and hf-mirror.com are reachable and were used instead for all dependencies and training data.
The first smoke-test launch failed on DOC_MASK_IMPL=varlen requiring ATTN_BACKEND=fa3 when only ATTN_BACKEND=sdpa was set; corrected launch parameters for the smoke test.
The second smoke-test launch failed with PermissionError from the /data mount-detection bug described above; fixed in lib.py.
limitations: check-setup was RED at the start of this period (reference-code drift from the prior session's edits) and remains unresolved pending a full re-reconciliation, which is now also required by the lib.py fix and the host change.

No gated experiment has been authorized or run this period. All infrastructure work (environment setup, tokenizer training, the lib.py fix) was necessary before any authorize-run call could succeed on the new host.

The contamination finding is reported at preliminary_observation strength rather than contradicted/supported because it has not yet been backed by a registered internal_run evidence record citing real run_ids; that registration is queued as part of the re-reconciliation work.
decisions: Do not hand-edit reconciliation.json's baseline field with the clean 0.929541 figure; that figure is itself weak-provenance direct-SSH evidence. Require a fresh, authorize-run-backed >=10-seed baseline measurement as part of full re-reconciliation.
Adopt the lib.py DATA_DIR fix as a portability correction, to be included in the re-reconciliation's reference-code digest.

Proceed with paper_021's Round 0 (a 5 GPU-minute instrumented timing screen) as the first authorized action once check-setup passes, since it is the highest information-per-minute action on the queue and can kill two of the six proposed mechanisms before any seed budget is spent.
Continue to forbid KNOB experiments this block per the plateau rule; the six paper_021 proposals are the only admissible next actions.

next_hour_plan.question: Once the environment and re-reconciliation are complete, does the n-gram sparse optimizer's state-decay block actually consume the predicted ~19ms per step, and does exact lazy-decay (paper_021 M1) recover it without changing the update mathematically?
next_hour_plan.why_now: This is the highest-provenance, lowest-risk proposal on the queue -- the predicted saving coincides with an already-measured, previously unexplained term in the campaign's throughput model, and the fix is mathematically exact rather than a quality gamble.
next_hour_plan.stop_condition: Abort before spending any seed budget if the Round 0 timer reads under 8ms for the decay block; otherwise proceed to the pre-registered falsifiers in paper_021 (>=3x block-time reduction, numerical equivalence at the renormalization boundary, paired n=3 improvement >=0.003).
